summary: Read materialized SCTA ST I q19 a3–5,7–8,10 and pinned Elwes Spinoza Ethics I definitions/axioms,16–17,29–33. Aquinas explicitly proposes self-determination of necessary will toward nonnecessary secondary objects (a3 ad5–6), distinguishes a cause of the single act from rational ordering of its objects (a5), and rejects secondary-cause defect as sufficient contingency explanation (a8). Spinoza I33 noteII grants will as essence for an internal objection: different complete decrees imply different actual intellect/will and hence essence. His freedom means action from own nature (definition7), not contingent choice. Rejected self-sufficiency-alone as proof of contingent willing, no-cause as no-object-reasons, temporal immutability as cross-world identity, and varying world-label tables as explanatory free creation. Detailed exact locators, strongest replies, rejected readings and remaining gaps persist in docs/notes/selected-effect-bridge-462.md, source follow-up. No new result, premise establishment or root-premise change.
blocker: Independently defend or refute whether a complete rational intentional specification can vary without an additional contingent intrinsic item, independent external determinant, or necessitation by the necessary act. This is an unproved proposed research fork, not certified coverage; intrinsic identity and intentional relations remain unmodeled.
